anomalies.observed: The ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch is implemented with T8 = AO3400A (drain on NET0088, which runs to the valve header H12/P3 and the V2 DIGITEN-24V load), while the AON6407 (T4) is instead placed at the input 'Reverse polarity protection' position on the 24 V rail. The two power MOSFETs are swapped relative to the intended roles.
anomalies.expected: The specification assigns the AON6407 (8-DFN) to the ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch and the small-signal AO3400A to the other discrete position: 'T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch' and §5 'r2 ... T3 AON6407, T5 AO3400A ×1'. The valve (a 24 V inductive solenoid) must be switched by the 8-DFN AON6407.

evidence.quote: T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch ... drives ATO_VALVE net
r2 drops to a smaller discrete-switch set (T1/T4 BT3904 ×2, T2 IRLR2905, T3 AON6407, T5 AO3400A ×1)
Page 1 / Page 3: 'T8 AO3400A' with drain on NET0088 feeding H12/P3 'ATO Valve' / V2 DIGITEN-24V; 'T4 AON6407' at the 'Reverse polarity protection' block on the 24 V input

anomalies.impact: The 24 V solenoid is now switched by a 30 V / SOT-23 AO3400A in a footprint designed for an 8-DFN AON6407 (footprint mismatch / cannot be assembled as drawn), and the part is marginal for the inductive kick and continuous valve current, risking thermal or avalanche failure of the ATO valve; conversely the reverse-polarity position uses the wrong package. The valve drive and input protection do not match the intended design.

anomalies.observed: The two float-switch bias resistors are placed on the opposite signals from the reference design: R5 (10 k) is a pull-UP to +3V3 on NET0011 (FLOAT_HIGH, IO1), and R37 (10 k) is a pull-DOWN to GND on NET0006 (FLOAT_LOW, IO0).
anomalies.expected: The specification's reference netlist puts the pull-up on the low float and the pull-down on the high float: 'R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k, R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k'. With the J4 connector wired VCC/HIGH/LOW/GND, this gives a pull-down on HIGH and a pull-up on LOW.

evidence.quote: R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k, R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k, R2 FLOAT_LOW /BPUMP 4.7k, R11 FLOAT_HIGH /BATO 4.7k
Page 1 'Safety Switches': R5 10k between +3V3 and NET0011 (HIGH); R37 10k between NET0006 (LOW) and GND

anomalies.impact: The pull directions are inverted relative to the float-switch wiring, so both water-level inputs are held at their pulled level and do not change when the floats actuate. The low-level pump cutoff and the high-level overflow/ATO interlocks (R48/R54 4.7 k to the pump/valve gates) would not respond to actual water level, removing the safety shutoffs.

parsed.summary: The build deviates from the intended r2 design: the ATO-valve and reverse-polarity power MOSFETs are swapped (AO3400A on the 24 V valve instead of the specified 8-DFN AON6407, a wrong-part/footprint error), and the two float-switch pull resistors are tied to the opposite signals than the reference netlist, which would freeze the water-level safety inputs. The LiDAR being wired and the environmental sensors being DNP are not reported, as the former contradicts a documented 'unwired' limitation in the opposite (benign) direction and the latter is an explicitly noted known limitation.
